anomalies.observed: The buck regulator U5 (TPS62933, the 24 V to 5 V converter that feeds the ESP32 and the AZ1117) has its EN pin (pin 2) marked as no-connect (`unconnected-(U5-EN-Pad2)`, pin type `input+no_connect`). Its other control pins are wired: RT (pin 1) to R32, SS (pin 7) to C17, FB (pin 8) to /0V8_{BK}, BST (pin 6) to C89. The EN pins of the three TMC2209 drivers, by contrast, are all tied to the ~EN net.
anomalies.expected: A regulator that powers the whole controller should have a defined enable state, either tied to VIN through a divider or pulled high or low, rather than left floating. The specification does not mention this, so the expectation comes from standard practice for this part.
anomalies.impact: If the EN input has no defined level, the 5 V buck may not start reliably or may behave unpredictably, which would affect the ESP32 and the 3.3 V LDO. This is low confidence because the part's EN pin may tolerate floating in this application.

parsed.summary: The netlist values for the feedback divider (52.3k/10k gives about 5 V), VREF dividers, sense resistors, TMC2209 coil and power wiring, isolator grounds and transistor pinouts are all consistent. The only candidate deviation is the unconnected enable pin on the 24 V to 5 V buck regulator U5, which is a low-confidence finding.
